--------
In this VladTV segment, Rex Holloway reflects on a failed taco poisoning plot aimed at former Aryan Brotherhood members housed alongside active members after prison officials separated “Circle” inmates from the Brotherhood. Holloway explains how the administration’s refusal to recognize ex-members created dangerous tensions inside solitary housing, where men who had quit still remained within reach of the gang. He also discusses “Wizard,” describing him as deeply committed to the cause and willing to carry out violent orders, though the person tasked with the poisoning ultimately backed out. The conversation touches on prison politics, loyalty, retaliation, and a dispute involving a stolen radio from a respected “general” that Holloway says escalated the risk. A stark look at prison gangs, true crime, and the consequences of correctional policy decisions.

Devonte “Dirt Rock” Lee sits down with VladTV for an uncensored look at his life as a Southside Compton Crip from Bird’s Lane and his connection to Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson, Big Dre, T-Brown “Bubble Up,” and Duane “Keefe D” Davis. Lee recounts growing up around Compton, the Lakewood Mall fight involving Trayvon Lane, Death Row Records tensions, Bad Boy, Diddy/Puffy rumors, and the fallout after Tupac Shakur was shot in Las Vegas following the Mike Tyson fight at the MGM Grand.

Dirt Rock also details his own federal drug case, working with investigators, Greg Kading’s Murder Rap, and being subpoenaed to testify in Keefe D’s Tupac murder trial. He reflects on street codes, cooperation, the deaths of Orlando Anderson and Big Dre, Snoop Dogg’s ties to their music label, and why Keefe D’s interviews may have changed everything.

Charleston White sits down with Vlad to break down Lil Durk’s recent not guilty verdict, the role of OTF Jam’s testimony, and what the decision could mean for the upcoming federal RICO case in Los Angeles. White clarifies that his online jabs at Durk have been trolling, saying he respects the changes Durk has made and doesn’t view him the same way he viewed King Von. The conversation also touches on OTF, Vonnie, THF Baisu, Quando Rondo, Lul Tim, and the tragedy surrounding Lul Pab. Vlad discusses due process, jury decisions, and why he accepts the courtroom outcome. White compares Durk’s legal situation to John Gotti Jr., predicts another win, and cites LA’s history with celebrity trials involving O.J. Simpson and Robert Blake. The interview also covers high-profile defense lawyers Drew Findling, Brian Steel, Bradford Cohen, Kodak Black, Lil Wayne, and hip-hop’s legal landscape.

Dale Comstock on Becoming Youngest Person Ever to Join Delta Force (Part 2)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 1: https://youtu.be/U21AbA_cZII
--------
Dale Comstock sits down with Vlad to break down how, at just 23 years old and 164 pounds, he was told he became the youngest soldier selected for Delta Force. The former Green Beret explains the brutal U.S. Army special operations selection process, where 110 candidates started, six finished, and only three were chosen. Comstock details the mindset required to survive ruck marches with heavy gear, psychological evaluations, and the “no second chance” rule for anyone who voluntarily withdraws. He also reflects on the pressure of joining an elite unit alongside operators a decade older, the daily demand to prove himself, and why passion, discipline, and purpose mattered more than size or ego. This conversation offers a rare look at Delta Force selection, Special Forces culture, military resilience, and life lessons from one of America’s most demanding units.

--------
Ramon “Mundo” Mendoza sits down with Vlad to explain how his undercover work against the Mexican Mafia blurred into real criminal exposure. Mendoza says he refused to wear a wire while helping law enforcement locate murder fugitives, prevent hits, and build 32 documented homicide and drug cases. To maintain credibility, he says he began selling heroin — eventually getting arrested near the 101 after leaving West LA’s Oakwood Apartments with two kilos, money, and guns.

He also discusses contacting Gil “Chili” Avila from L.A. County Jail, bailing out through Mexican Mafia-connected bondsmen, and the dangerous fallout from a bank robbery shootout involving Gabby, Richie, Sapo, and Stony. Mendoza then revisits being pulled into the Bob Moretti homicide plot in Signal Hill while still operating undercover, raising difficult questions about policing, informants, organized crime, and accountability.

Iconic Video Vixen Gloria Velez Tells Her Life Story (Flashback)
recentItems.description:
In this flashback, we revisit Gloria Velez as she shares her tumultuous journey from Long Island to Brooklyn, opening up about her dysfunctional family life, her father’s addiction, and her mother’s struggles. At 14, Velez entered the music industry, performing at teen clubs and touring with DJ Laz and 2 Live Crew. She also detailed her experience of abuse by singer Aaron Hall, who was 16 years her senior, including physical violence and mental manipulation, as well as her fight for custody of her son.

Velez went on to transition into modeling and music, recounting her experiences working with Hype Williams, Jay Z, and other prominent artists and industry figures. She also addressed her public falling out with VladTV over creative differences and financial issues, which led to a temporary rift. The conversation concluded with Velez promoting her book, Silent Screams, which details her life experiences and time in the entertainment industry.
